s01.text: You were told a diamond means forever. That is not an ancient tradition. It was a sales line.

s02.text: Before the nineteen thirties, most engagements in America did not involve a diamond at all.

s03.text: In 1938, De Beers hired the advertising agency N.W. Ayer to change what the stone meant to people.

s04.text: In 1947, a copywriter named Frances Gerety wrote four words: a diamond is forever.

s05.text: The line ran for decades, until a written campaign stopped sounding like an advertisement and started sounding like something your family had always known.

s06.text: The two months salary rule is often blamed on the same campaign. Historians dispute that part, so leave it aside.

s07.text: You can still buy the ring. Just know which part was inherited and which part was sold.
